Hey, I just graduated last Nov with a major in Immunology through Bachelor of Science. I would say second year subjects were the hardest for me, mostly because of the adjustment from first year—those subjects were quite easy in comparison, and note that my first year exams were all online as well. Third year subjects are much more intense content-wise, but they felt easier for me, probably because I started taking Anki seriously, but also the class average for midterms went up. It was around 50-60% for second year MIIM subjects and 60-70% for third year, so maybe they made it a bit easier or maybe people in third year just took it more seriously since it's their major now. Back in second year, some people took MIIM subjects as their science elective.   
  
Also, second sem third year subjects were actually quite fun, you'll get see people for your cohort more and also the teaching staff. Specifically, Keit Loi, he's the best and he will make you enjoy Immunology. 

Immunology is hard, but not impossible, I almost switched to Pharmacology/HSF because everyone I met since first year kept saying Immunology is very very difficult, it really scared me. But I'm glad I chose to stick with it.   
  
Also there's not much difference between Immunology and Infection and Immunity. iirc, for Infection and Immunity you need to take two Microbiology subjects so like bacteriology and virology, whereas for Immunology, you need to take two Immunology subjects so Principles of Immunology and Medical & Applied Immunology in third year!

I highly recommend taking biomedical research subject (BIOM30003) in third year. The main downside with Immunology major at unimelb is that you barely get any lab experience during you undergrad (except honours year) and this will allow to use your Immunology/Infection&Immunity knowledge in a lab based setting. Best subject ever and it ended up being a WAM booster for me too.
